data.content_ref: inline:The target requires a 'documented correction event' (a pivot from an incorrect initial intuition to a correct answer forced by the checklist) as the signature of genuine reliability gain. This conflates the presence of a saved error with the existence of reliability gain. A panel may perform reliably because the checklist prevents the error from ever arising (e.g., the panel never forms an incorrect intuition because the checklist front-loads the correct variable); absence of a correction event would then falsely imply 'compliance luck' even though reliability is genuine.
